meta.title: Onsoo Botanicals: entering the US market in 2027
meta.subtitle: Whether to enter, and by which route; for decision at the March 2027 board meeting
meta.purpose: Decide whether to enter the US in 2027 and by which route
meta.confidentiality: Synthetic benchmark data; company and figures are fictional

inputs.label: Onsoo Botanicals US market entry briefing pack (synthetic data)

storyline.governing_thought: Onsoo should enter the US in 2027 through Amazon, the only route within the board's limits, and gate the launch on ad cost

exec_summary.text: The US is worth entering: K-beauty drove 39% of US facial skincare growth, and the Amazon pilot nearly doubled its sales

sub_points.text: K-beauty sales rose 89% in 2021–25, six times other brands' growth
Pilot buyers rebuy at 29% within 90 days, near the 31% peer benchmark

exec_summary.text: Only Amazon-led fits the board's limits: retail-led breaks the cash cap, and Japan stays small

sub_points.text: Retail-led needs $20.8M by 2030 and cuts 2027 group margin to 4.5%
Japan pays back by 2029 but adds only $7M of revenue in 2030

exec_summary.text: The retail case rests on weak assumptions: newcomers like Onsoo sell 2.6 units per door a week, not 4.5

sub_points.text: The leading retailer removes newcomers selling under 4.0 units a week
The 0.71 correlation behind the halo fits doors following online sales

exec_summary.text: Amazon-led pays back by 2030 only if ad cost stays below 28.6% of sales, so approve it with gates

sub_points.text: At the 32% ad cost of scaling peers, payback slips past 2030
Raise the retail trigger from 15% to 20% awareness

next_steps.action: Approve Option A, with the ad-cost gate (ACoS at or below 29%) and the $10M and 20% awareness retail triggers
Set up the US entity, MoCRA registration and English labels; take over the listings from the cross-border seller
Rebuild the US plan at 28% and 32% ACoS and at 25% duty, with per-SKU economics for the four new SKUs
Prepare the cost response if the mid-2027 tariff decision raises duty to 25%
Re-run the awareness survey and report ACoS against the gate

lead_message.text: K-beauty brands are the growth engine of US facial skincare, capturing 39% of its growth in 2021–25

slides.rationale: Mix of a market over five years -> stacked-column; growth multiple in sidebar

sidebar.caption: of the category's growth in 2021–25 came from K-beauty brands
bullets: **K-beauty brands:** sales up 89% since 2021, six times the growth of other brands, lifting their share from 9% to 15%
**Other brands:** still most of the market, but their sales grew only 15% over the four years
**For Onsoo:** $26M of US sales in 2030 would be under 1% of what K-beauty sold in 2025, so market size is not the limit

footnotes: A 2026 trade-press figure of $5.2B for the 'US K-beauty market' also counts makeup and hair care; it is not comparable and is not used
Onsoo 2030 sales from the planning team's Amazon-led volumes (section 2)

lead_message.text: The Amazon pilot shows real demand, with monthly units nearly doubling in six months and buyers returning at the peer rate

lead_message.text: The Amazon halo behind Option B is unproven, because the 0.71 correlation also fits brands earning doors after winning online

slides.rationale: Qualitative argument with three strands of evidence -> text-columns

columns.header: A correlation cannot show which way the effect runs
detail: Retailers invite brands that already sell well online, which produces the same link
Brand size alone can drive both doors and Amazon sales
The memo gives no test that separates these from a halo

columns.header: The one peer with scale in both channels grew online first
detail: Saebom added 300 retail doors only in 2025, after building its Amazon business
Its doors followed its online sales, the reverse of the memo's claim
So the 1.3 times halo in Option B has no measured basis

columns.header: Buyers find new brands online, not in stores
